chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abu Ali ibn Rashid said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I am your ransom, indeed a woman from our family had a boy fall ill, and she said: O God, if You relieve him of it, so-and-so is free, and the girl is not well-versed (in distinguishing which is better). So which is better? I am your ransom, should she free her, or spend her price in ways of piety?' He said: 'It is not valid except her freeing (the slave).'

key_terms.أَيُّمَا أَفْضَلُ: Which of the two is better
key_terms.فُلاَنَةُ: So-and-so (referring to a specific but unnamed individual)
key_terms.وُجُوهِ الْبِرِّ: Ways of piety / channels of charity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a person makes a conditional vow to free a slave but is unsure which slave is intended?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic principle that a conditional vow of manumission (‘itq) requires the actual freeing of the slave, rejecting the alternative of paying their value in charity (kaffarah or sadaqah). It highlights the distinct legal status of ‘itq vows compared to other types of vows, emphasizing the tangible liberation of the bondwoman as the primary fulfillment of the promise.
